::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** [July 1868][^1]  
**Manuscript:** MS Westcountry Studies Library, Exeter/ Yonge 1867/ 3
:::

My dear [Miss Smith](people/person_263.qmd)
Thanks for the [Exhibition](other_books/otherbook_531.qmd) - which is full of interest. I wish there was any chance of my seeing it. I like most of what you have said much, though I do not agree with your deprecation of [Dr Hook](people/person_709.qmd)’s character of Edward VI, for certainly his own journal does not bear out the praises bestowed on him, and it was rather forward to say the least of it in a mere boy to meddle with the convictions of learned men. Thanks much for the whole - it is pleasant reading-

[*The rest of the letter is missing*]

---

[^1]: The paper has been cut about to remove the signature, address and date.

**Note:** A. Carter Smith’s article ‘National Portrait Gallery’ appeared in *MP* 1868 (2): 65. Walter Farquhar Hook wrote *The Three Reformations* (1847), *Lives of the Archbishops of Canterbury* (1862) and *A Church Dictionary* (1864, 9th ed.)
